morgan: Ran an nsys profile against the dedicated pool reproducer (seq=2048, batch=8) on gfx nodes. Quick summary: attn_kv_lookup dominates at ~42% self time, kv_cache_eviction at ~18%, softmax at ~12%. nvtx markers around request lifecycle included.
perf-bot: automated-summary: top_kernels=["attn_kv_lookup:42.3%","kv_cache_eviction:17.6%","softmax:12.1%","matmul_256:8.4%","other:19.6%"], total_gpu_time=23.4s, active_sm_util=68% avg. trace: /perf/traces/2854321000.ns
aditya: can you paste the exact nsys command and the workload params? curious about warm vs cold KV hit rate.
morgan: command was:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_2854321000 --trace=cuda,cublas,nvtx -t cuda,nvtx python -m reproducer --seq 2048 --batch 8 --requests 500
```
KV hit stats from our instrumentation: overall hit_ratio ~0.68, but eviction spikes correlate with p50 spikes; cold-window eviction_rate ~0.21 for first 50 requests.
sara: ok this smells like eviction + serialized prefetch. Can you run a perfetto microtrace around a single request that triggers eviction? NVTX zones placed at KV lookup/insert would help. also try nvprof for kernel timelines for that request.
aditya: did you try bumping batch size? larger batches can amortize kernel launch overhead and change kernel mix.
morgan: quick experiment: batch=16 on same run -> total_gpu_time drops to 19.2s and attn_kv_lookup share falls to ~28%, but p99 latency went from 210ms -> 480ms which breaks SLO. so batching helps throughput but hurts tail latency.
kai: theory: our kernel selector currently picks q_kernel_v1 for all kv paths when quantized. q_kernel_v1 uses a small-thread-block strategy that is eviction-friendly but high per-request overhead. q_kernel_v2 (wider blocks) exists but we avoid it for seq>512 due to memory register pressure. proposal: selector rule: if seq>=1024 and batch<=8 prefer q_kernel_v1; else for seq>=512 && batch>=16 prefer q_kernel_v2. also add an adaptive path that switches after warmup when kv_hit_ratio>0.75.
```
// pseudo-diff
if (quantized) {
  if (seq >= 1024 && batch <= 8) use(q_kernel_v1);
  else if (batch >= 16 || kv_hit_ratio >= 0.75) use(q_kernel_v2);
}
```
perf-bot: note: switching kernels may change SM occupancy; q_kernel_v2 measured +12% SM util on pilot nodes but also +6% register usage.
sara: agree with adaptive switch, but we need guardrails: metrics-based hysteresis (min 200 requests warm window) and failback on p99 regressions. also add CI microbench for both kernels with seqs {128,512,1024,2048} and batch {1,8,16}.
aditya: we should also check whether kv_cache_eviction kernel runtime is dominated by host-device memcpy or device-side eviction logic. the nsys flame shows small memcpy spikes right before eviction kernel on some samples.
morgan: captured a short perfetto slice with nvtx markers: https://perfetto/trace/2854321000 (linked). the flame shows eviction kernel launching in bursts that coincide with single-request spikes.
kai: follow-ups: i'll prototype selector change in a branch and add telemetry hooks for kv_hit_ratio and eviction_rate. can someone create the CI microbench and a small repro for eviction cold-window? assigning to aditya for repro + sara for trace collection.
aditya: will do repro + run nvprof/nvtx traces across batch sweep (1,4,8,16) and seq sweep (512,1024,2048). i'll post outputs here.
sara: i'll add perfetto templates and the CI cases. also we should label kernels in traces with selector version so future comparisons are easier.
morgan: thanks — action items: (1) kai: draft selector PR with adaptive switching & hysteresis, (2) aditya: repro + batch/seq sweep traces, (3) sara: perfetto templates + CI microbench. aim to have initial data in 48h. :hourglass_flowing_sand: :thumbsup:
